risk_notes: sqlite3 CLI is invoked without a pinned version; supply chain integrity depends on whatever system package provides it.

Input SQL file is redirected into sqlite3 via shell '<' redirection; if an attacker controls sql/cleanup_database.sql, arbitrary SQL (including ATTACH/load_extension if enabled) would be executed against sakila.db.

Script runs PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON and BEGIN IMMEDIATE then performs bulk DELETE/UPDATE across payment, rental, inventory, film_actor, film_category, actor, category, language, country, city, address, staff, customer, and film — destructive operations with no backup step documented.
VACUUM is run after COMMIT outside the transaction; if interrupted, database may be left in a partially-cleaned state with no rollback.
No checksum/signature verification is documented for sakila.db or the cleanup script.
No container image, package manager manifest, curl|bash, pip install, or npm install patterns were found in the provided output, so no third-party package CVEs apply to this artifact.
